correctness.rationale: The rank-r tangent/normal decomposition is exhaustive and orthogonal. Both projectors equal identity on the tangent summands, leaving only N=(I-UU^T)Z(I-VV^T). On N the difference has three mutually orthogonal blocks UCN, ND^TV^T and -UCND^TV^T. Their squared norms add and simultaneous norm attainment uses N=ab^T with maximizing right singular vectors of C and D, proving the exact gamma law for all finite dimensions, including one-sided zero cases. For an epsilon embedding, compress H-I to the pair formed by x=A^-1By/||A^-1By|| and unit normal y; (a-1)^2+b²<=epsilon² and b=a||A^-1By|| maximize exactly at a=1-epsilon². Applying independent sharp one-sided inequalities to the three blocks gives the claimed coefficient. The 2x2 Gram H_e has eigenvalues 1±e, giving equality for each epsilon pair; exact rational checker verifies nontrivial witnesses. The source projector derivation was independently reconstructed; no finite evidence was used for infinite quantification.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 DLRA paper explicitly demonstrates that oblique sketch Galerkin can respond badly to the perpendicular residual and asks which embedding conditions control discrepancy. This theorem answers a natural exact instantaneous stability problem: a computable pair of one-sided normal-to-trial defects combines with a sharp three-block law, and embedding tolerances have a necessary-and-sufficient worst-case accuracy frontier. The coefficient is attained for arbitrary distortion pairs and is not merely another pessimistic bound. The result clarifies concrete sketch dimension/quality requirements on the combined trial-plus-realized-normal spaces. It does not allege global trajectory bounds or probabilistic OSE guarantees.
